answer: Agents join via an opal-bonded identity registry that stores a crystal behavioral fingerprint of each agent's past task outputs. Random peers later mirror those outputs by re-running the same sealed prompts and comparing digests; a mismatch freezes the identity and burns the opal bond. Spawning many fakes therefore means paying a full bond and sustaining consistent real compute for every mirror audit, which erases the cheap-sybil advantage.
